objective.performance: the engine's composite score on sim/config.json scoreWeights, 0-100
objective.friendly: 100 * (0.6*winRateFloorNorm + 0.4*podFunScoreFor). A 60% win rate is a HARD CEILING, enforced as a constraint on the final build rather than priced into the score; below 35% is penalised quadratically.
objective.enjoyment: 100 * (0.5*funScoreFor + 0.5*decisionDensity/78). 78 is D3 Atraxa's count, so the number is comparable to the ones already quoted.
objective.cost: dollars actually spent, at 0.025 objective points a dollar -- the rate at which a free bench card 90% as good as a $20 card wins any swap worth under five points.

confirmation: Every accepted swap re-measured at 8 seeds x 25,000 games against the pre-move list on the same seeds; kept only when the paired objective gain exceeded 2*hypot(seA, seB).
note: Recommendations, not applied. Every swap was confirmed at eight seeds by twenty-five thousand games, paired against the list it changed, and kept only when the difference beat twice the pooled standard error.

engineArtefacts.note: Found by sweeping the whole 2,014-card pool for the engine's known blind spots, not by noticing a suspicious result. Each is proved by a pair of lists differing only in the thing under test. Cards in these classes were barred from ever being swapped IN; cards already in a deck were left alone.

reminderText.what: classifyCard reads Scryfall's parenthetical reminder text, which carries no rules meaning.
reminderText.scale: 29 cards across the six decks change classification when parentheticals are stripped; scores move -1.07 to +1.75 and win rates -8.77pp to +2.56pp.
reminderText.worst: Bronze Guardian (D4). Ward's reminder text says 'counter', and it sits in the same sentence as 'Double strike', so doubl(e|ing)[^.]*counter matches and the deck-wide +1/+1 counter doubler is set. The card has no counter interaction at all.

counterDoublerAppliedFree.what: Aetheric Amplifier really does double counters, but only for {4} at sorcery speed; prepareDeck applies a doubler free, every turn, deck-wide.
counterDoublerAppliedFree.outcome: Left uncorrected, and the search cut it on its own — it is a three-mana rock in a deck with five counter cards.

gatedTreasureReadAsFree.what: makesTreasureFreely accepts a bare {T} cost, so Currency Converter reads as a one-mana Treasure engine. The real card needs a card discarded, exiled with this artifact, and for it to be a land.

measured.units: score points lost when the Treasure clause is removed

fetchLandsReadAsUntapped.what: producedColors credits a fetch with every colour it can name and entersTapped is read off the fetch itself, so Naya Panorama models as an untapped R/G/W land. The real card taps for {C}; a colour costs {1}, the land, and arrives tapped.

xDropped.what: parseManaCost ignores {X} entirely, so Kozilek's Command ({X}{C}{C}) prices as a two-mana instant that both ramps and removes.

colourlessPipAsGeneric.what: {C} is not in COLORS, so a colourless pip falls through to generic and any land pays it. D5 and D6 have two colourless sources between thirty-odd lands.

givesItselfAway.what: A permanent that hands itself to an opponent after one use (Hithlain Rope, Humble Defector) models as one that stays yours.

underCredited: damage amplification and team anthems (Moonshaker Cavalry)
'create X tokens where X is …' reads as one token
opponent-spell taxing (Rhystic Study) reads as a near-blank
two instants of the same mana value in the same role are indistinguishable
engineArtefacts.repaired: Three of these are no longer artefacts: reminder text is stripped before a card is classified, a fetch land enters tapped because the basic it gets arrives tapped, and a Treasure locked behind a condition inside an activated ability is not ramp. This block records the run as it was made, against the engine as it then was; the bars it describes were what kept those cards out of these recommendations.

contention.rule: Each deck searched against the whole bench. Where more decks wanted a card than there are physical copies, the copy went to the deck with the larger MARGINAL value for it — the deck's objective with the card, less the same deck with its own basic in that slot, both at eight seeds by 25,000 — and the losers re-searched with it blocked, repeating until nobody was fighting. The swap's own gain is the wrong measure: D5's Currency Converter swap was worth +6.1, but essentially all of that was getting rid of Aetheric Amplifier.
contention.frozenAfterTier0: A copy awarded at $0 is off the table for every other deck at $15 and $40, because the brief's own order is bench before buys and a later block cannot undo the $0 list a deck already starts from.
